studyMetadata.title: Test Style
studyMetadata.description: Stress tests responsive styling for participant-facing form elements.

response.prompt:
# Layout Stress Test

Resize the browser to inspect how form elements respond to long prompts, long option labels, and unusually large option sets. Every response on this page is optional.

## Long-form content

This intentionally long paragraph checks that text wraps within the response area instead of creating a horizontal scrollbar. It includes aVeryLongUnbrokenIdentifierThatShouldStillWrapWithinTheAvailableParticipantViewportWithoutExpandingThePageBeyondItsBounds.
Enter a short response for a question whose prompt is deliberately much longer than the input value participants are expected to provide.
response.secondaryText: The prompt and supporting text should wrap while the input retains a reasonable maximum width.
response.infoText: The information icon should retain a consistent size even beside a long prompt.

response.prompt: Describe what happens to this textarea and its label as the available width becomes narrow.
response.secondaryText: The textarea should shrink with the viewport without stretching indefinitely on wide screens.

response.prompt: Choose an option from a dropdown containing labels of very different lengths.
options: An intentionally long dropdown option label that should remain readable without widening the form indefinitely

options.label: An option with additional information
options.infoText: This tooltip also checks the size and alignment of the information icon.

response.prompt: Choose from many buttons with mixed label lengths. The buttons should wrap into additional rows as space becomes constrained.
options: A considerably longer fifth option label

response.prompt: Horizontal radio options with several long labels.
options: A long radio option that needs to wrap
The final and longest radio option in this group

response.prompt: Horizontal checkbox options with mixed content lengths.
An eleven-point Likert scale with long endpoint labels.
Dense matrix-radio example with seven columns and long row and column labels.
response.secondaryText: Each row accepts one response. Resize the viewport to inspect wrapping and control alignment.
questionOptions: The interface remains understandable when the available horizontal space is limited
Long question labels wrap without obscuring their associated controls
Column headings remain distinguishable when several answer choices are present
The selected radio option remains visually associated with the correct row
